expectedFailures.notes: Trigger: injected (the test fails on purpose). Permanent canary proving the manifest mechanism works on every run.

expectedFailures.messagePattern: F7: Start Jam had no effect after an undo whose restore failed
expectedFailures.notes: Trigger: injected (a listener throws during the undo restore). Pilot test. Fails while an exception during undo leaves restoreRunning set.
Trigger: injected (a listener throws while Start Jam is in progress). Start Jam is left half-applied: in a jam with the jam clock stopped.

expectedFailures.messagePattern: F12: the latest change was not autosaved
expectedFailures.notes: Trigger: injected (another process holds the newest autosave file open, as antivirus or sync tools do). Windows only; SKIPPED elsewhere. Expectation is provisional pending the autosave-semantics decision.

expectedFailures.messagePattern: F13: state from the rejected newest autosave leaked
expectedFailures.notes: Trigger: injected (the newest autosave holds a value this version cannot parse, e.g. written by a newer version or damaged). Entries that exist only in the rejected file survive the fallback. Expectation is provisional pending the autosave-semantics decision.

Trigger: natural (clients connecting and disconnecting while the scoreboard changes, as tablets do on venue Wi-Fi). Rate depends on the machine; baseline measured on Linux (0.42-0.53 over four runs of 200 iterations).

expectedFailures.messagePattern: F6: a Timeout press from another device 1.2 s later started a second timeout
expectedFailures.notes: Trigger: natural (SBO and JT both react to one timeout whistle; the JT's press arrives 1.2 s after the SBO's). Phase 2 pilot. A fix needs commands to carry the state the operator saw, since a deliberate re-timeout looks the same on arrival.

expectedFailures.messagePattern: F6: a Stop press from another device 600 ms after a Timeout press deleted the timeout
expectedFailures.notes: Trigger: natural (the SBO calls a timeout during a jam; the JT, who saw the jam end, presses Stop 600 ms later). Different buttons within 1 s are treated as one operator correcting a mistake, so the timeout is undone.

expectedFailures.messagePattern: F10: a repeated \+1 trip point frame was applied twice
expectedFailures.notes: Trigger: injected (a retry delivers the same frame twice). Needs request IDs, or equivalent, in the protocol.

Trigger: natural (ten devices reconnect at once, as when venue Wi-Fi comes back). Over-the-wire view of the Phase 1 fan-out race: the ConcurrentModificationException refuses WebSocket handshakes. Baseline measured on Linux (50 rounds of 10).

expectedFailures.messagePattern: F17: an uploaded plain file was written outside the media folder
expectedFailures.notes: Trigger: injected (a hostile upload from a device with write access). validFileName uses String.matches, which never matches a name containing ../

expectedFailures.messagePattern: F17: an uploaded zip file was written outside the media folder
expectedFailures.notes: Trigger: injected (a zip whose entry name climbs out of the media folder: zip slip).

expectedFailures.messagePattern: F1: a wall-clock step of \+5 min then -5 min moved the game clocks
expectedFailures.notes: Trigger: natural (NTP correcting the laptop's clock, or someone fixing it, during a jam). Needs libfaketime (Linux, macOS) or -Dreliability.allowClockChanges=true (Windows); SKIPPED otherwise.
